name: Sapo National Park
subtitle: Sapo National Park is a protected rainforest in south-east Liberia, declared a national park in 1983 and managed by the Forestry Development Authority.

facts.label: Status and founding
facts.value: Liberia's oldest and largest protected area, established 1983

facts.label: Managing agency
facts.value: Forestry Development Authority (FDA), with Fauna & Flora and the Wild Chimpanzee Foundation as key partners

facts.label: Corridor
facts.value: Part of the transboundary Tai-Grebo-Krahn-Sapo conservation corridor between Liberia and Cote d'Ivoire

facts.label: Threats (FDA)
facts.value: Hunting, illegal artisanal gold mining and other human intrusions

facts.label: Staffing
facts.value: The FDA notes inadequate staff to manage the park effectively

facts.label: Location
facts.value: South-east Liberia, about 70 km inland from the coastal town of Greenville

facts.label: Habitat
facts.value: Forest composition: 63% primary and mature secondary forest, 13% swamp-forest, 13% seasonally inundated forest

facts.label: Settlement and hunting
facts.value: No permanent human settlements inside; hunting pressure thought to be high

facts.label: Encroachment before the war
facts.value: Two major encroachments: a logging company in 1985 and farmers in 1986

facts.label: Since the war
facts.value: Illegal logging and alluvial gold mining have occurred

parts.text: Sapo National Park is a protected rainforest in south-east Liberia, declared a national park in 1983 and managed by the Forestry Development Authority. It covers 180,363 hectares and is part of a transboundary conservation corridor with Cote d'Ivoire. Hunting and illegal gold mining are named as threats.
